When `handle_audit_routing.py` finds no deterministic-pattern proposals AND `[audit_interpretation].enabled = true`, the no-proposals branch invokes `audit_interpretation.interpret_audit(client, context)`. Severity info/warn/error/critical maps to ntfy Priority + Tags. Fail-safe: never raises, never hangs beyond the curl timeout.

Best-effort durable record (#706): appends the redacted Alert + AlertResult delivery outcome AFTER delivery — records the fault even when ntfy delivery failed (a failed POST is still a recorded fault). Holds an exclusive lock so concurrent emitters cannot tear a record. A ledger problem never changes the returned AlertResult or raises. Date-partitions pruned past 30 days.

flows.name: felix-canary
flows.purpose: Deterministic component-health scanner (Foundation 1 / Epic #516): evaluate every service-inventory health_check per ADR-0006 and alert on stale/failed/un-evaluable live components via the #701 bus. Zero LLM in the tick path.
flows.trigger: felix-canary.timer (systemd --user, OnUnitActiveSec=15min, OnBootSec=5min, Persistent=true); also manual `systemctl --user start felix-canary.service`

path.description: ~15-min cadence. felix-canary.service declares OnFailure=felix-canary-onfailure.service.
One full pass. WorkingDirectory=/home/claude/kg-automation; EnvironmentFile=-/home/claude/.config/felix/alert-bus/env for FELIX_ALERT_NTFY_TOPIC.

Reads every service-type entry's declared health_check + status. A component becomes a canary target purely by declaring a health_check — no separate registry file. NON_SERVICE_TYPES (python-module/library/cli-integration) are exempt.

ADR-0006 gate-before-probe: only status in {active,running} is probed; a suspended/deprecated/planned/retired component is recorded `suppressed` and never probed. Freshness probes compare the pointer's authoritative timestamp to max_age_seconds; liveness probes check http/shell/systemd-status. A live component with no usable health_check is a coverage `gap` (no-silent-drop). Fail-open: a raising probe becomes `unknown`, never aborts the pass.

source=felix-canary:<component_id>. Dedup keyed on component_id + last_outcome: any transition emits (incl. recovery INFO); failed/stale (ERROR) page immediately then once per 6h window; unknown/gap (WARN) are recorded but page only once persistent past the window. Only emitting outcomes reach the bus; healthy/suppressed/deduped are ledger-only.

One line per component per tick recording EVERY outcome (healthy/stale/failed/suppressed/gap/unknown/deduped), evidence, whether it emitted, and evaluated_at (FR-008). A ledger-write fault records an errors[] entry and never aborts the pass.

Aggregate tick-signal — the runner's own health pointer (FR-010): status, completed_at_utc, components_evaluated, emitted, suppressed_dedup, coverage_gaps, suppressed_status, errors, duration_ms. Registered as the runner's own freshness health_check so #269 can watch the watcher.
Dedup state: component_id -> {last_outcome, last_emitted_utc}. Drives once-per-window paging + the failed->healthy->failed transition guarantee. Fail-safe: a missing/corrupt file loads empty.

Fires ONLY when felix-canary.service exits non-zero — a runner-level fault (inventory unreadable, state dir unwritable). Independent of the runner's own emit logic, so a runner that crashed before it could report is still surfaced (SC-006). felix-trust-scan lacked this crash detector.

flows.name: intake-validation-loop
flows.description: Tier-1 task-intake validation loop (#749). Rides each inbox-processing tick: after route_and_finalize, felix-admin-capture runs scripts/intake/scan_inbox.py (kent READ via vikunja-api-kent per ADR-0007) which resolves the Inbox project id via the #748 vikunja_refs seam, enumerates not-done tasks, classifies Tier-1 completeness (project ≠ Inbox + a friction f:1-3 + an Eisenhower q:*), writes an immutable per-digest correlation record + latest pointer + per-tick observability artifact under /data/services/openclaw/state/intake/, and emits one numbered WhatsApp digest of the incomplete tasks and their missing fields. Kent replies in compact shorthand; the main DM agent correlates the reply content-based (line-number set + task-title evidence, habits correlate_reply_to_checkin semantics) to the right digest and invokes scripts/intake/apply_reply.py, which resolves tokens through the seam and applies project + labels + applicable Tier-2 via the kent WRITE token (vikunja-api-kent, now the sole runtime Vikunja token per ADR-0007 — the same kent identity the scan reads under, collapsing the former #715 two-token model; the retired felix-bot path 403'd on kent-owned label attach, which this closes — #750). Writes are read-modify-write with family-replace for the mutually-exclusive q:/f: families; a per-line ApplyResult (applied/echoed_back/noop/overload_flagged/not_found/already_done/moved_conflict/access_denied) is appended to the apply ledger and confirmed to Kent. Deterministic throughout; the LLM is a narrow fallback only for a token the parser cannot resolve, constrained to a canonical name re-resolved through the seam (Directive 6). Applying a working project + f: + q: moves the task out of Inbox so it stops re-appearing (re-prompt-until-resolved, no suppression state).

Immutable per-digest correlation record {digest_id, created_utc, created_et_date, source_cron, entries:[{n, task_id, title, missing_fields}]}; latest.json pointer. Records past the 48h window are expired (habits parity).

Deterministic parse (scripts/intake/shorthand.py) + seam resolution + apply plan; per-line status. LLM fallback only for an unresolved token.
Applies working project + f: + q: + applicable Tier-2 (due: ET-EOD). felix-bot is never used for the kent-owned label attach — closes #750 (SC-008). Task leaves Inbox and stops re-appearing.
Per-line ApplyResult ledger (FR-014). Main confirms the per-line outcomes to Kent.

flows.name: crontab-capture
flows.description: Hourly capture of the claude crontab into Restic-backed-up storage, so a destroyed crontab is recoverable from a snapshot rather than from a security-monitor drift baseline. The recovery leg is manual and rare: a human reads the artifact during an incident. Nothing reinstalls it automatically -- that would be a reconciler, which is #890's subject.

path.note: Read as bytes, never text: universal-newline translation and locale decoding would break the byte-identity promise for the stored body.
Atomic tmp+os.replace; rewritten only when the body changed, so the backup sees no churn. Refused on an empty, failed, or >50%-truncated read.
Written on every run including refusals, so a dead capture is reported rather than assumed working. Read by felix-canary.

Implicit: /data/services is already a Restic source path, so no source-set change was needed. Adding /var/spool/cron instead would have split the snapshot path-group (restic forget runs with no --group-by) and permanently stranded the existing snapshots from pruning.
/etc/restic/password is root-only, so restoring is an operator step, not an agent step.
